$comment: Single source of truth for the EQ 6-tier role model + permission matrix. Extracted from eq-shell src/session.ts + src/permissions/**. Edit this file and run `npm run build` to regenerate roles.ts / roles.json. Adding a tier, permission, or roleAlias is a spec-level change — keep IDENTITY-MODEL.md in sync.

roles.label: Manager
roles.description: Full access. Manages people and access groups, undoes changes, deletes records, approves quotes, and sees every report.

roles.label: Supervisor
roles.description: Runs the day-to-day. Views and edits records, runs and confirms imports, manages workers, licences, rosters and dispatch, creates quotes, and sees cost, margin, rates and supplier logins. Cannot manage user accounts, open reports, undo changes, or delete records.

roles.label: Employee
roles.description: Everyday staff access. Views records, quotes, maintenance, equipment and field information, and can start an import. Cannot see personal details, hours, licences, cost or margin.

roles.label: Apprentice
roles.description: Read-only across records, maintenance, equipment and field information. Can see imports but not start one, and cannot view quotes.

roles.label: Labour Hire
roles.description: Agency worker. Sees field information and the equipment list, nothing else.

roles.label: Subcontractor
roles.description: External trade engaged for a job, not an agency worker. Sees field information only.

platformAdmin.effect: Orthogonal to role. When true, can() short-circuits to true for every permission across every tenant. EQ-internal staff only (single audit point for cross-tenant power).

$labels: label = short plain-English name for admin UIs (what a non-technical manager reads when granting access). description = the longer developer-facing explanation. Keep labels verb-first and jargon-free per EQ voice.
$deprecated: Optional `deprecated` string on a permission = scheduled for removal in a future major bump, kept only so existing tenant_role_overrides / consumers don't break early. State the reason + the replacement. Build still emits the key; a lint/tooling pass can warn on new usage.

permissions.label: View users
permissions.description: See everyone who can sign in to your organisation, with their role and status.

permissions.label: Invite users
permissions.description: Send someone an invitation to join and set up their sign-in.

permissions.label: Edit users
permissions.description: Change someone's name or contact details. Changing their role or permanently deleting them are their own separate permissions.

permissions.label: Deactivate users
permissions.description: Switch off someone’s access so they can no longer sign in. Their records are kept.

permissions.label: Review onboarding
permissions.description: Review and approve the details a new worker submits when they join, before they're added as staff.

permissions.label: Manage access groups
permissions.description: Create access groups and choose who belongs to them. Groups add permissions on top of someone’s role.

permissions.label: View activity log
permissions.description: See what changed, who changed it, and when.

permissions.label: Undo changes
permissions.description: Reverse a change shown in the activity log, putting the record back as it was.
permissions.deprecated: The undo action does not currently work — the system always refuses it. Kept only so nobody's existing access breaks; do not grant to anyone new. Bring this back once undo is rebuilt.

permissions.label: View records
permissions.description: See customers, sites, contacts, and assets. Personal contact details are controlled separately.

permissions.label: See personal details
permissions.description: See someone’s phone number, date of birth, and emergency contact. Kept separate from viewing records so people can look up a customer or site without seeing personal information.

permissions.label: Add records
permissions.description: Add a new customer, site, contact, or asset.

permissions.label: Edit records
permissions.description: Change the details on an existing customer, site, contact, or asset.

permissions.label: Delete records
permissions.description: Permanently remove a customer, site, contact, or asset. This cannot be undone.

permissions.label: Show records in Field & Service
permissions.description: Choose whether a site or customer appears in EQ Field and EQ Service.

permissions.label: View imports
permissions.description: See imports that have been started and how they went.

permissions.label: Start an import
permissions.description: Upload a spreadsheet, match its columns, and check it for errors — without saving anything yet.

permissions.label: Confirm an import
permissions.description: Save a checked import into your live records. This overwrites existing data and cannot be undone.

permissions.label: View equipment
permissions.description: See the plant and equipment list, including calibration dates.

permissions.label: Edit equipment
permissions.description: Add equipment, change its details, or update calibration dates.

permissions.label: View reports
permissions.description: Open the management reports.

permissions.label: See financial reports
permissions.description: See the cash, cost, and margin figures inside GM Reports. Kept separate from reports.view so a security group can grant someone reports without also handing them the money.

permissions.label: Upload reports
permissions.description: Upload a source file that reports are built from.

permissions.label: Generate AI briefing
permissions.description: Produce the AI-written summary of recent activity.

permissions.label: Open Cards
permissions.description: Open the worker onboarding app.
permissions.deprecated: No longer used. EQ Cards is switched on for a whole organisation rather than per person. Existing settings still work — do not apply this to anyone new.

permissions.label: Submit onboarding
permissions.description: Fill in or manage a worker’s onboarding details.
permissions.deprecated: No longer used — “Review onboarding” does this job. Existing settings still work — do not apply this to anyone new.

permissions.label: View maintenance
permissions.description: See work orders, faults, and scheduled maintenance.

permissions.label: See job pricing
permissions.description: See what a job is worth — its price and contract value. Kept separate from viewing maintenance so people can do the work without seeing the money.

permissions.label: Raise work orders
permissions.description: Raise a new work order or report a fault.

permissions.label: Close work orders
permissions.description: Mark a work order as finished.

permissions.label: Reopen a work order
permissions.description: Reopen a work order that was already closed. Kept to a small group so the activity log stays meaningful.

permissions.label: Log calibration results
permissions.description: Record calibration or test results against a piece of equipment.

permissions.label: Receive calendar digest
permissions.description: Get the daily email summarising upcoming and overdue calendar items. Manager only by default — add anyone else via the "Calendar Digest Recipients" group so the rest of the recipient list stays a deliberate, curated choice.

permissions.label: View field information
permissions.description: See staff, licences, availability, and job assignments in EQ Field.

permissions.label: See timesheets & hours
permissions.description: See the hours workers have logged. Kept separate because hours affect pay.

permissions.label: See worker licences
permissions.description: See workers’ licences and tickets, and whether they are current.

permissions.label: See charge rates
permissions.description: See what labour-hire workers are charged out at.
permissions.deprecated: Labour-hire rates are actually controlled by ops.view_rates, in both the app and the database — this key is never checked. Kept only so nobody's existing access breaks; do not grant to anyone new. Use ops.view_rates instead.

permissions.label: Dispatch staff
permissions.description: Send staff to jobs and shifts.

permissions.label: Build & edit the roster
permissions.description: Build and change the crew roster. Separate from day-to-day dispatch because it sets the plan rather than following it.

permissions.label: Manage worker licences
permissions.description: Add a worker’s licence or confirm you have sighted it. This is a sign-off — it records that someone checked.

permissions.label: Manage labour-hire companies
permissions.description: Add or change the labour-hire companies you use and what they charge.

permissions.label: Add / remove / edit workers
permissions.description: Add a worker, change their details, remove or restore them, and reset their PIN.

permissions.label: View quotes
permissions.description: See quotes and their status. Cost and margin are controlled separately.

permissions.label: Create quotes
permissions.description: Write a new quote or change an existing one.

permissions.label: Approve quotes
permissions.description: Approve a quote and send it to the customer.

permissions.label: View rates & pricing setup
permissions.description: See what labour-hire agencies charge, and open Setup — where pricing, the rate library, quote templates, and estimators are configured.

permissions.label: See cost & margin
permissions.description: See what a job costs and what you make on it. Kept separate from viewing quotes so people can work on a quote without seeing the margin.

permissions.label: Manage rates & pricing setup
permissions.description: Add, import, or change labour-hire rate cards and the pricing setup.

permissions.label: Convert quote to a job
permissions.description: Turn an accepted quote into a numbered job. Job numbers are entered by hand, so this is a deliberate commitment step.

permissions.label: View suppliers directory
permissions.description: See the list of trade suppliers, wholesalers, and hire companies.

permissions.label: Manage suppliers directory
permissions.description: Add, change, or remove entries in the suppliers list.

permissions.label: See supplier login/password
permissions.description: See the account login and password saved against a supplier. Kept separate so people can use the supplier list without seeing stored passwords.

permissions.label: View documents
permissions.description: See the document library, and the documents assigned to you to read or sign.

permissions.label: Manage documents
permissions.description: Upload document versions, archive documents, and add, rename, or delete categories.

permissions.label: Require a sign-off
permissions.description: Push a document to a role, crew, or person so they must read or sign it, and see who has and who hasn't completed it yet.

permissions.label: Change someone's role
permissions.description: Set or change what role a person holds — wherever that happens, including through EQ Cards.

permissions.label: Permanently delete a user
permissions.description: Permanently delete a person's account. This cannot be undone.

permissions.label: Edit imported records
permissions.description: Change a record that came in through an import, archive or dismiss a duplicate, or work the review queue.

permissions.label: Carry out and record work
permissions.description: Run test procedures and record their results, and raise an on-site check, in EQ Service.

permissions.label: Archive or delete reports
permissions.description: Archive a reporting period, or permanently delete one and its job rows. This cannot be undone.

permissions.label: View the daily briefing
permissions.description: See the daily AI-written activity summary, and dismiss or mark your own action items done. Manager and supervisor only — the brief names workers alongside their licence numbers and expiry dates, and includes quote and pipeline dollar values.

permissions.label: Use AI tools
permissions.description: Use the AI assistant, ask questions about jobs and licences, and run licence-photo recognition.

roleAliases.$comment: Foreign role vocabularies mapped onto canonical EqRole. Build validates every target is a real role. INVARIANT: no alias targets is_platform_admin — cross-tenant power is never derived from a tenant-held role, so tenants stay isolated. EQ-internal platform ops live out-of-band (service-role / audited impersonation), not in any tenant role.

service.label: EQ Service
service.description: EQ Service (CMMS) tenant_members.role -> canonical EqRole. super_admin maps to a tenant-scoped manager (NOT is_platform_admin); supervisor is a direct match; technician is an employee; read_only is a read-mostly apprentice.

$defaultGroups: Canonical starter security groups for seeding a fresh tenant (which today starts with zero). A group is a named bundle of EXTRA PermKeys, ADDITIVE on top of a user's base role (surfaced as session.extra_perms) — NOT a role. These templates intentionally grant only CROSS-CUTTING perms (held by a few people regardless of role) and never duplicate what a role already grants. Build validates every `perms` entry is a real permission key and that keys + names are unique. EQ Shell seeds DEFAULT_GROUPS on tenant creation. Names/descriptions are plain English (what a manager reads).

defaultGroups.name: Equipment editors
defaultGroups.description: Edit the plant & equipment list and calibration details. Add people here who maintain equipment but whose role normally only lets them view it.

defaultGroups.name: Report viewers
defaultGroups.description: View GM reports without being made a manager. Add supervisors or leads here who need to read reports.

defaultGroups.name: Project Managers
defaultGroups.description: Manage users, review Cards onboarding, and view the audit log without full manager admin rights. Promoted from a tenant-specific group (originally SKS) once it proved to be a common cross-cutting need, not a one-off.
